candidates.eligibility_note: NMN/NR are SUPPLEMENTS, not approved drugs -> INELIGIBLE as a Track-2 approved medication; nicotinamide is also a supplement AND directionally opposite (sirtuin inhibitor). The approved prescription product on this axis, niacin (nicotinic acid, extended-release Rx tablets; adult dyslipidemia label), is evaluated separately as C-NA (added 2026-10-19). This branch entry keeps the mechanism judgment; C-NA carries the product-level eligibility.
candidates.best_evidence: North BJ et al., EMBO J 2014, PMID 24825348 (SIRT2 deacetylates BubR1-K668). NOTE: NMN experiments were in aging/WT/Sirt2-null contexts; BubR1^H/H lifespan used a SIRT2 TRANSGENE. NMN untested in the MVA model. Counter-evidence: nicotinamide (sirtuin inhibitor) lowered BubR1 in North 2014 Fig 1 — NAD-pathway molecules are NOT interchangeable.
candidates.disposition_reason: On-mechanism rationale is real, but the NMN/NR drug step is a bridging hypothesis unvalidated in the MVA model and in N1002K; oncology direction contested (raise BubR1 suppresses vs NAD+ fuels tumors).
candidates.decisive_experiment: In patient/isogenic N1002K cells: NAD+ precursor dose-response -> BubR1-K668 acetylation + total BubR1, mitotic timing, aneuploidy; PLUS clonal-fitness/transformation arm for the tumor-fuelling concern.

candidates.branch: C functional-compensation (NAD+ -> SIRT2 -> BubR1-K668 deacetylation / stabilization)
candidates.eligibility_note: Approved prescription product: niacin extended-release tablets (US, DailyMed label revised 12/2025, checked 2026-10-19; setid 6e604319-e164-4056-ab80-b78b98c519c7), indicated for dyslipidemia in adults. Pediatric Use (label, verbatim): 'Safety and effectiveness of niacin therapy in pediatric patients (<= 16 years) have not been established.' Pediatric path = off-label, specialist-supervised use in severe pediatric hypercholesterolemia (Colletti 1993, PMID 8516088: 21 children aged 4-14; adverse effects in 76%, reversible aminotransferase elevation in 29%, discontinuation in 38%). ELIGIBLE as an approved medication; NOT an approved pediatric indication — this is why the research judgment is CONDITIONAL, not SUPPORTED.

gates.G1_oncology: contested: raising BubR1 is tumour-suppressive in mice (Baker 2013), NAD+ supply is pro-tumour in some models -> contradictory
gates.G2_pediatric: no pediatric label; off-label specialist experience with frequent adverse effects = credible but not clean path

candidates.best_evidence: CHAIN (all measured): Suijkerbuijk 2010, PMID 20516114 — in biallelic MVA patient cell lines BUBR1 abundance is low, the checkpoint is impaired, and ECTOPIC BUBR1 RESTORES CHECKPOINT ACTIVITY; MVA mutations split into an abundance-lowering class (truncating transcript loss + high turnover of missense mutants, which 'consistently occur in or near the kinase domain') and a function-lesion class. Suijkerbuijk 2012, PMID 22698286 — that domain is a pseudokinase: catalysis is dispensable, ATP-pocket residues govern conformational stability, so a substitution there destabilises rather than inactivates. North 2014, PMID 24825348 — NAD+/SIRT2 deacetylates BubR1-K668 and raises BubR1 abundance in vivo; SIRT2 transgene extends BubR1-H/H lifespan. Pirinen 2020, PMID 32386566 — niacin raised blood NAD+ up to 8-fold in adults. COUNTER-EVIDENCE: Wu 2023, PMID 38009412 — SIRT2 overexpression on a WILD-TYPE background does not affect health or lifespan, so the axis is specific to a BubR1-low setting and carries no general-longevity support. No study reports NAD+ status in MVA or BUB1B-mutant cells (PubMed, 2026-10-19), so the deficiency the drug would correct has not been shown to exist. nicotinamide (sirtuin inhibitor) LOWERED BubR1 in North 2014 — NAD+ vitamers are not interchangeable. Ferrell 2024, PMID 38374343 — 4PY and cardiovascular events in adults.
candidates.disposition_reason: The only approved prescription product on the SIRT2-BubR1 axis, and the axis now rests on patient-cell evidence that raising BUBR1 restores the checkpoint in this disease (20516114) plus a structural account of why a kinase-domain missense lowers abundance rather than catalysis (22698286). What remains unbridged is the drug step: no NAD+ booster has been tested in MVA or on this allele class, NAD+ status in MVA is unmeasured, there is no pediatric label, and the oncology direction is unresolved. Named CONDITIONAL candidate from 2026-10-19 (replaces 4-PBA); a hypothesis for follow-up, not a recommendation; holds only in scenario S1.
candidates.decisive_experiment: Patient-derived fibroblasts or LCL vs isogenic (CRISPR-corrected) or healthy control, with a BubR1-knockdown positive control: NAD+-precursor dose-response (niacin, NR, NMN; nicotinamide as the wrong-direction control) -> total BubR1 and K668 acetylation (western / IP), nocodazole arrest index and mitotic timing (live imaging), lagging chromosomes / micronuclei / single-cell aneuploidy, with cell death, proliferation and clonal fitness measured in the same wells; N-terminal antibody for a truncated product (S3). >= 3 biological replicates, blinded scoring. REJECT if BubR1 does not rise or the checkpoint does not recover, or if aneuploid-cell survival or proliferation increases.

candidates.eligibility_note: ataluren lost approval (EMA non-renewal 2025-03-28; PTC withdrew FDA NDA application 2026-02-12); aminoglycosides INELIGIBLE here on renal grounds; ELX-02 investigational; DAP preclinical
candidates.best_evidence: Trzaska 2020 Nat Commun PMID 32198346 (DAP UGA readthrough); Toledano 2024 Nat Genet PMID 39174735 (genome-scale readthrough). Full-length restoration precedent is CFTR (Sharma 2021 PMID 34272367), not BUB1B.
candidates.disposition_reason: Corrected: readthrough gives a near-full-length product (old 'truncated' reason withdrawn). Coordinates recomputed (readthrough_coordinates_2026-10-08.md): stop UGA at c.2209-2211, +1 context base = c.2212 (raw log's c.2213 was off by one). Blocker = NMD (PREDICTED, not measured; needs allele-specific mRNA) + no renal-safe approved UGA agent. One-allele rescue judged by functional threshold, not allele count.
candidates.decisive_experiment: Allele-specific BUBR1 mRNA + full-length protein under NMD-inhibition alone / readthrough agent alone / combination, with SAC-competence readout.

candidates.eligibility_note: approved for urea-cycle disorders; pediatric (glycerol form >=2 months)
candidates.best_evidence: Mechanism = COPII/secretory-cargo export, NOT a cytosolic chaperone (Ma W & Goldberg J, eLife 2017, PMID 28594326 (verified 2026-10-19: 'ER retention is imposed by COPII protein sorting and attenuated by 4-phenylbutyrate', eLife 2017)). Zero BUBR1-specific data.
candidates.disposition_reason: Mechanism mismatch (BUBR1 is cytosolic/mitotic) + achievable exposure (0.2-1.3 mM total) overlaps the HDAC range. Thresholds are NOT a measured N1002K ECx -> 'direct rescue and exposure feasibility not established' (deprioritized), NOT 'no window proven'. Demoted from named candidate to INSUFFICIENT consistently across report, pitch, candidate table and submission record on 2026-10-19; the named conditional candidate is C-NA.
candidates.decisive_experiment: In-cell EC50 for N1002K-BUBR1 stabilization across 0.05-10 mM vs a histone-H3/H4-acetylation (HDAC) readout in the same cells.

candidates.eligibility_note: ELIGIBLE only as the Rx drug product (Acetadote/acetylcysteine solution), NOT an OTC NAC supplement.
candidates.best_evidence: As a disease modifier: rejected (effective 0.5-5 mM vs reachable plasma ~2-25 uM oral). As mitigation: reduces oxidative/senescence load (consequence endpoint).
candidates.disposition_reason: Conditional as downstream mitigation (a lane the strategy permits), NOT a disease modifier; exposure for the mitigation endpoint unproven; keep tumor-promotion watch.
candidates.decisive_experiment: In patient cells: ROS + senescence markers (SA-beta-gal/p16/p21) + proliferative lifespan at achievable exposure; explicitly a mitigation readout, not a fidelity fix.

candidates.drug: AMPK aneuploid-deselection (metformin; non-renal AMPK agent needed)
candidates.eligibility_note: Eligible instance = metformin (approved; pediatric >=10yr; FDA renal limit by eGFR). A non-renally-cleared AMPK activator would be preferable but none is approved.
candidates.best_evidence: Tang YC et al., Cell 2011, PMID 21315436 — p53-RELATED apoptosis (Fig 3), AMPK-dependence (Fig 4), Bub1b^H/H MEFs (Fig 6). NOT p53-independent.
candidates.disposition_reason: Research question: under what cell + exposure does a selective effect exceed normal-tissue loss? Anti-proliferation is not repaired segregation. Euploid cells in constitutional BUB1B deficiency still carry the defect.
candidates.decisive_experiment: Euploid-vs-aneuploid differential viability in matched patient cells with a non-renal AMPK agent; measure normal-cell loss and p53 status; separate selection from fidelity.

candidates.best_evidence: Baker 2011 Nature PMID 22048312 used the INK-ATTAC GENETIC tool + AP20187 to clear p16 cells — this is NOT evidence that the D+Q DRUG rescued the disease model. Zhu 2015 Aging Cell PMID 25754370 D+Q is in Ercc1-deficient/other models. No aneuploidy endpoint in any cited study.
candidates.disposition_reason: Acts downstream; genetic-tool validation != D+Q drug evidence; endpoint mismatch (senescence markers, not aneuploidy) + toxicity on this child's organs.
candidates.decisive_experiment: Only re-enters if a patient model shows D+Q reduces the PROLIFERATING aneuploid clone fraction (scDNA-seq/micronucleus) AND does not accelerate outgrowth.
